_about: Pops (PRD, "M3 Demand" and "Turnover"). Set by M3-01 for the issues after it to read; each issue that reads a field may change it and says so. Every value here is a starting value with no source behind it, to tune in M3-21, except `childrenLeaveYears`, the one turnover number the PRD fixes. `popSizeCap` is the most people one pop may hold, for a home of density 1, 2 and 3 in order, so a house is one pop and a tower of 1,000 is ten or more (M3-03). `newcomer` is who moves to the city: the share at each education level, the share that has children, and for a home of density 1, 2 and 3 in order the least and most people a newcomer household holds, drawn evenly between them and cut to the room the home has left, and the satisfaction a newcomer starts at (M3-08). `graceDays` is how many game days a newcomer's workers are left out of the residential bar's unemployment while they look for work, counted down once a game day by the pops' sweep and carried to both parts of a pop that splits (#361, PRD "Four demand bars"). It must stay below the month a newcomer with no job takes to leave, so a town with no jobs reads its own unemployment before its first newcomers give up. A newcomer's wealth follows the land value of the home it takes, from `newcomers.wealth` in landvalue.json (M3-25). The most is never above `popSizeCap`. `workerShare` is the share of a pop's people who work, lower when it has children (M3-03). `turnover` holds yearly rates for M3-11, each turned into a chance per pop per game day by dividing by 365. Births and deaths are per person, so a pop's daily chance is the rate times its size over 365, and a tower pop of 100 sees a hundred times a house's. `childrenLeaveYears` is how long a pop has children on average: its daily chance that a child grows up and leaves is 1 over 365 times it, and when that happens the pop loses a person and no longer counts as having children. `replacementsPerPopYear` is per pop, the share of households replaced a year. Each pop gets one draw a game day, which gives it at most one of the four events, replacement, death, a child leaving and birth in that order (M3-11). A home takes a newcomer household only while its room left fits the least of `newcomer.size` for its density, so the places deaths free in an apartment or tower wait for a household rather than taking pops of one (M3-11). `satisfaction` sets each pop's score once a game day (M3-10, PRD "Satisfaction"). M3 has one input, the job: `target` is where the score heads for a pop with nobody who works, one in a job at its own education level, one in a job below it, and one with workers and no job. Each day the score moves `dailyShare` of the way to its target, rounded to the nearest point and at least one. A pop whose score has stayed below `leaveBelow` for `leaveAfterDays` game days in a row moves out, so a newcomer at 50 with no job leaves after about a game month, and a worker at 70 who loses a job a few days later. `satisfaction.displacement` is the hit displacement gives (M4-10, PRD "Eminent domain"): each expropriation record within `radius` metres of a pop's home takes `neighbours.perPerson` points for each person it displaced, all of them together at most `neighbours.most`, and a pop the city displaced takes `own.base` plus `own.perPerson` for each person its old home held, at most `own.most`, wherever it moved. Both fade in a straight line to nothing over a game year. A pop whose owner redeveloped its home takes `own.byOwnerShare` of its own hit, and its neighbours none. The caps together leave a pop in a job at its level above `leaveBelow`, so displacement alone sends away only a pop that is already unhappy. A pop whose home is removed is displaced (M3-12, PRD "Removing things"): `displacedPerTick` is the most displaced pops placed in new homes in one tick, the rest waiting in a queue for the ticks after. No prices here, so no source years.
